about: The muscles of the chest wall: the three intercostal layers, the deep muscles inside and behind the cage, and the pectoral and serratus muscles on its outside, drawn from the model's own ribs, cartilages, sternum, clavicle, scapula and humerus. Skeletal muscle: the drives are muscle tone (rigidity and paralysis), a seizure, shivering, ventilation for the external intercostals and respiratory drive for the muscles of forced breathing. The intercostals rise with the ribs in the breath. Each space is a schematic strip and the direction of the fibres is not drawn; the thickness of each layer is a drawing choice.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Intercostal Muscles
parts.summary: The three layers of muscle between the ribs
parts.function: They fill the spaces between neighbouring ribs in three layers and move with the ribs in breathing. Drawn schematically, one strip per space; the direction of the fibres is not drawn.

drives.note: Guyton and Hall name this muscle among those that raise the ribs or sternum in a deeper breath, so a rise in minute ventilation engages it. The weight is a display scale.

Guyton and Hall name this muscle among those recruited when breathing is driven harder (accessory inspiration or forced expiration), so a rise in central respiratory drive engages it. The weight is a display scale.
Raised skeletal muscle tone (rigidity) is a rise in the tone of the muscles of the body, so this muscle tightens with it. The weight is a display scale.
Lost skeletal muscle tone (paralysis, or a neuromuscular blocker) lowers the tone of the muscles of the body, so this muscle goes slack. The weight is a display scale.
A seizure is a brief, intense motor discharge, which the engine reports as 0 or 1; skeletal muscle contracts in it. The weight is a display scale.
Shivering is rhythmic contraction of skeletal muscle in the cold, so this muscle is engaged by it. The weight is a display scale.

parts.label: External Intercostals
parts.summary: The outermost layer
parts.function: They run from the tubercle of each rib to its costochondral junction and lift the ribs in quiet inspiration.

parts.summary: The middle layer
parts.function: They run from the angle of each rib forward, between the cartilages of the upper spaces, and draw the ribs down in forced expiration.

parts.label: Subcostales
parts.summary: Thin bands on the inner surface of the lower ribs
parts.function: They cross one or two ribs near the angles and act like the internal intercostals. Three bands are drawn.

parts.label: Transversus Thoracis
parts.summary: The muscle behind the front of the chest wall
parts.function: It arises from the back of the lower sternum and fans out to the inner surfaces of the costal cartilages two to six, and draws them down.

parts.summary: Twelve pairs of small muscles at the back of the ribs
parts.function: They run from the transverse processes of the seventh cervical and upper eleven thoracic vertebrae to the rib below and lift the ribs.

parts.label: Pectoralis Major
parts.summary: The large muscle of the front of the chest
parts.function: It runs from the clavicle, sternum and upper cartilages to the humerus and moves the arm. Breast tissue lies over it; the breast organ draws that.

drives.note: Exercise engages the muscles that move and steady the trunk and hip, so a rise in exertion engages this muscle. The weight is a display scale.

parts.label: Clavicular Part of Pectoralis Major
parts.summary: The upper part from the clavicle
parts.function: It arises from the medial half of the clavicle.

parts.label: Sternocostal Part of Pectoralis Major
parts.summary: The large middle part
parts.function: It arises from the front of the sternum and the upper costal cartilages.

parts.label: Abdominal Part of Pectoralis Major
parts.summary: The lowest fibres
parts.function: They arise from the sheath of the rectus abdominis.

parts.label: Pectoralis Minor
parts.summary: A smaller muscle deep to the pectoralis major
parts.function: It runs from the third to fifth ribs to the coracoid process of the scapula and draws the scapula forward and down.

parts.label: Serratus Anterior
parts.summary: The muscle on the side of the chest under the scapula
parts.function: It runs from the upper ribs to the medial border of the scapula and holds the scapula against the chest. In forced breathing it helps to lift the ribs.

parts.label: Superior Part of Serratus Anterior
parts.summary: The upper part, from the first two ribs
parts.function: It runs to the superior angle of the scapula.

parts.label: Intermediate Part of Serratus Anterior
parts.summary: The middle part
parts.function: It fans from the second and third ribs to the medial border of the scapula.

parts.label: Inferior Part of Serratus Anterior
parts.summary: The lower part, from the lower ribs
parts.function: It converges on the inferior angle of the scapula.
